Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Empty bottles can be recycled.

payload.snippet: A cardboard box is empty.
options: Flatten it and put it in recycling
Leave it in the middle of the room
payload.explanation: Flattened cardboard takes less space in the recycling bin.

payload.snippet: The newspaper is finished.
options: Put it in the paper recycling
Put it in the food bin
Tear it up and leave it
payload.explanation: Paper can be recycled many times.

payload.snippet: A glass jar is empty.
options: Rinse it and put it in the glass bin
Throw it in the regular bin
Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Clean glass jars can be recycled.

payload.snippet: An empty tin can is on the counter.
options: Put it in the metal recycling
Throw it at the bin and miss
Leave it open on the counter
payload.explanation: Tin cans are recyclable metal.

payload.snippet: A plastic bottle is half full of juice.
options: Pour out the juice, rinse it, then recycle it
Put it straight in recycling with juice inside
Pour the juice in the food bin
payload.explanation: Food left in containers can contaminate recycling.

payload.snippet: Mia has a pile of old magazines.
options: Put them in the paper recycling bin
Put them in the general bin
Leave them in the rain outside
Tear out pages and leave them on the floor
payload.explanation: Old magazines are recyclable paper.

payload.snippet: A broken toy is made of all plastic.
options: Put it in the plastic recycling
Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Clean plastic toys can often be recycled.

payload.snippet: The family has finished a box of cereal.
options: Flatten the box and put it in recycling
Put it in the food bin because it had cereal in it
Leave the box full of crumbs in the cupboard
Throw it in the regular bin
payload.explanation: Cereal boxes are cardboard — they can be recycled.

payload.snippet: There is an empty egg carton.
options: Throw it in the food bin
Put the carton in the garden
payload.explanation: Cardboard egg cartons are recyclable.

payload.snippet: Ben has a pile of drawings he no longer wants.
options: Put them in the paper recycling
Throw them in the regular bin
Put them in the food bin
payload.explanation: Used paper can be recycled into new paper.

payload.snippet: An aluminium drink can is empty.
options: Crush it lightly and put it in metal recycling
Put it in the plastic bin
payload.explanation: Crushed aluminium cans take less room in the recycling bin.

payload.snippet: A plastic shopping bag is old and torn.
options: Put it in a plastic bag recycling point
Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Some supermarkets have plastic bag recycling points.

payload.snippet: Zoe has finished her yoghurt pot.
options: Rinse it and check if it can be recycled
Throw it in the food bin with leftover yoghurt
payload.explanation: Rinsing food containers helps them be properly recycled.

payload.snippet: An empty cardboard tube is on the floor.
options: Put it in the paper recycling
Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Cardboard tubes from kitchen rolls are recyclable.

payload.snippet: A used envelope is on the desk.
options: Remove any plastic window then put in paper recycling
Leave it sealed and post it again
Put it in the food bin
Throw it in the regular bin
payload.explanation: Paper envelopes can be recycled if the plastic window is removed.

payload.snippet: Empty pizza boxes are piled on the table.
options: Check for grease — recycle clean sections or put oily ones in food waste
Throw them all in the regular bin
Leave them on the table for days
Put them all in paper recycling regardless of grease
payload.explanation: Greasy cardboard can contaminate paper recycling — clean sections can still be recycled.

payload.snippet: An old catalogue is on the shelf.
options: Put it in the paper recycling
Put it in the food bin
payload.explanation: Catalogues and junk mail can be recycled with paper.

payload.snippet: Sam has empty toilet roll tubes.
options: Put them in the cardboard recycling
Throw them in the regular bin
Put them in the food bin
payload.explanation: Cardboard toilet roll tubes are recyclable.

payload.snippet: Lily has a collection of used plastic straws.
options: Check if the council collects plastic straws
Throw them all in the garden
Put them in the food bin
payload.explanation: Plastic straw recycling varies by area — check local guidance.

payload.snippet: The cookies are ready in the oven.
options: Put on oven gloves before opening it
Open the oven with bare hands
Wait for someone else to do it
payload.explanation: Oven gloves protect hands from burns.

payload.snippet: The dough needs mixing.
payload.explanation: A spoon mixes dough safely.

payload.snippet: Mia drops an egg on the floor.
options: Tell a grown-up and help clean it up
Put the broken egg in the batter
Hide the shell in the batter
payload.explanation: Broken eggs on the floor are slippery — clean them up safely.

payload.snippet: The butter needs softening.
options: Leave it out on the counter for a bit
Put it in the oven at full heat
Heat it in the microwave too long
Hold it over the stove flame
payload.explanation: Room temperature softens butter gently.

payload.snippet: The cake batter needs pouring into a tin.
options: Hold the bowl carefully and pour slowly
Throw the batter into the tin
Pour it from very high up
Let go of the bowl with both hands
payload.explanation: Slow pouring keeps batter in the tin.

payload.snippet: Sugar and flour need measuring.
payload.explanation: Measuring cups give the right amounts.

payload.snippet: The muffins are too hot to eat.
options: Wait for them to cool down
Blow on them and eat immediately
Put them in the freezer for one second
Eat them straight from the tin
payload.explanation: Hot food needs time to cool.

payload.snippet: The recipe says crack two eggs.
options: Crack them on the bowl edge gently
payload.explanation: Gentle cracking keeps shell out of the batter.

payload.snippet: Ben's sister wants to help sprinkle icing.
options: Pour all the icing on at once himself
Tell her she will do it wrong
Run away with the icing bag
payload.explanation: Sharing baking tasks is fun for everyone.

payload.snippet: The dough is too sticky to roll.
options: Add a little flour to the board
Add water to make it stickier
Hit it with a rolling pin very hard
payload.explanation: A dusting of flour prevents dough from sticking.

payload.snippet: The timer goes off but the cake looks pale.
options: Ask a grown-up to check if it needs more time
Take it out because the timer said so
Put it on full heat for one minute
payload.explanation: Timers are a guide — an adult checks doneness properly.

payload.snippet: Lily wants to try the batter.
options: Ask Mum if it is safe to taste first
Eat a big spoonful straight away
Eat it while no one is looking
payload.explanation: Some batters contain raw egg — always ask an adult before tasting.

payload.snippet: The chocolate chips need melting.
options: Ask a grown-up to help melt them safely
Put them in the oven while it is very hot
Melt them over a flame alone
payload.explanation: Melting chocolate needs adult supervision.

payload.snippet: Tom gets flour on the kitchen counter.
options: Wipe it up with a damp cloth
payload.explanation: Cleaning up as you go keeps the kitchen safe.

payload.snippet: The cake is stuck in the tin.
options: Use a blunt knife around the edges first
Pull it out hard from one side
Shake the tin upside down violently
Eat it straight from the tin
payload.explanation: Loosening edges before turning out a cake prevents it breaking.

payload.snippet: The dough needs kneading for five minutes.
options: Push and fold the dough rhythmically
Leave it alone and hope it kneads itself
payload.explanation: Rhythmic kneading develops the gluten structure in bread dough.

payload.snippet: Zoe wants to decorate the cupcakes.
options: Spread the icing on with a spoon or knife
Squirt it directly from the tube at her brother
Put all the sprinkles on one cupcake
payload.explanation: Spreading icing evenly makes every cupcake look good.

payload.snippet: The recipe asks for a pinch of salt.
options: Use two fingers to pick up a tiny amount
Pour the whole salt shaker in
Skip the salt since it is a tiny amount
Use a teaspoon of salt instead
payload.explanation: A pinch means a tiny amount between two fingertips.

payload.snippet: The brownies need cooling before cutting.
options: Wait until they are completely cool
Cut them while hot and they crumble
Put them straight in the fridge for one minute
Eat them from the tray with a fork
payload.explanation: Warm brownies crumble when cut — cooling makes clean squares.

payload.snippet: Sam spills milk while measuring it.
options: Wipe it up right away before it spreads
Leave it and see if it dries
payload.explanation: Spills cleaned immediately prevent slipping and sticky residues.

payload.snippet: Mia wants to plant a seed.
options: Dig a small hole with her finger
Throw the seed on the ground
Plant it upside down in the air
payload.explanation: Seeds need to be in soil to grow.

payload.snippet: The seedling needs water.
options: Use a hose on full power
payload.explanation: Gentle watering with a small can doesn't flatten seedlings.

payload.snippet: Tom's pot plant is dry.
options: Check the soil with a finger first
Pour lots of water in quickly
Leave it in the rain only
Give it juice instead of water
payload.explanation: Checking the soil prevents overwatering.

payload.snippet: A seed packet says plant in spring.
options: Wait until spring to plant it
Plant it whenever you feel like it
payload.explanation: Seeds grow best when planted at the right season.

payload.snippet: The flower pot has no drainage holes.
options: Ask an adult to make some holes
Fill the pot with rocks instead of soil
payload.explanation: Drainage holes prevent roots from sitting in water.

payload.snippet: Lily puts too much soil in the pot.
options: Remove some so the plant has room to grow
payload.explanation: Plants need space to grow in their pots.

payload.snippet: A plant's leaves are turning yellow.
options: Ask a grown-up what is wrong
payload.explanation: Yellow leaves can mean different things — an adult can help diagnose.

payload.snippet: Ben finds a worm in the garden soil.
options: Leave it alone — it helps the garden
Pull it out and throw it away
Put it in the flower pot inside
payload.explanation: Worms improve soil by aerating it.

payload.snippet: The seeds need labelling.
options: Write the plant name on a lolly stick
Guess which is which after planting
Draw a tiny picture on each seed
payload.explanation: Labels help you remember what you planted.

payload.snippet: A sunflower is growing too big for its small pot.
options: Move it to a bigger pot or the garden
Cut the roots to make it fit
Tie the roots into the pot
Put a lid on the top of the pot
payload.explanation: Plants need space for roots to grow.

payload.snippet: Zoe's herb pot has no sunlight.
options: Move it to the sunniest windowsill
Buy a lamp for the herbs
Paint the walls white to reflect light
payload.explanation: Most herbs need sunlight to grow well.

payload.snippet: The soil in the garden feels very hard.
options: Add water and let it soften
Stamp on it to break it up
Use a kitchen knife to cut it
Leave the seeds on top of hard soil
payload.explanation: Softening soil first helps seeds to germinate.

payload.snippet: A carrot is ready to pull from the ground.
options: Grab it and yank hard from one side
Dig it out with a spade roughly
Cut the top off and leave the rest underground
payload.explanation: Gentle straight pulling avoids breaking the carrot.

payload.snippet: Sam's seedlings are very crowded in the tray.
options: Thin them out so each has space
Leave them crowded — the strongest will survive
Water them more to make space
Pull out all but one seedling
payload.explanation: Thinning seedlings gives the strongest ones room to grow.

payload.snippet: A new plant needs staking because it is leaning.
options: Tie it gently to a bamboo cane
Push it upright with your hands every day
Leave it leaning until it falls over
payload.explanation: Staking supports weak or tall plants.

payload.snippet: The lawn is long and needs mowing.
options: Tell a grown-up the grass needs cutting
Pull each blade of grass by hand
payload.explanation: Lawn mowers are adult tools — tell an adult when the grass is long.

payload.snippet: Ella plants a seed but nothing grows after two weeks.
options: Read the packet to check how long it takes
Plant ten more seeds on top
payload.explanation: Some seeds take many weeks to germinate — check the packet.

payload.snippet: A slug is eating the lettuce leaves.
options: Tell a grown-up who can put down slug pellets safely
Pour salt directly on the lettuce
Spray the plant with washing-up liquid
payload.explanation: Slug control needs adult guidance to be safe for the plant.

payload.snippet: Oscar waters his plant but the water runs straight through the pot.
options: Check whether the soil has become very dry and compacted
Water it again ten minutes later
Put the plant in a bucket of water to soak
payload.explanation: Water running straight through can mean the soil is too dry to absorb — soaking is sometimes needed.

payload.snippet: The plant is getting too much sun and the leaves look scorched.
options: Move it to a spot with indirect light
Water it more to cool it down
Cover it with a cloth all day
Leave it since sunlight is always good for plants
payload.explanation: Some plants prefer indirect light — scorched leaves signal too much direct sun.

payload.snippet: The dog's water bowl is empty.
payload.explanation: Dogs need fresh water available all the time to stay healthy.

payload.snippet: The cat is scratching at the litter box.
payload.explanation: A dirty litter box makes cats uncomfortable; cleaning it keeps them happy.

payload.snippet: The hamster wheel is squeaking loudly.
options: Put a tiny drop of oil on the axle
payload.explanation: A little oil stops the squeak so the hamster can run quietly at night.

payload.snippet: The fish tank is getting cloudy.
options: Cover the tank with a cloth
payload.explanation: Changing part of the water removes waste and keeps the fish healthy.

payload.snippet: The puppy is whining by the door.
options: Take the puppy outside for a walk
Let the puppy into the kitchen
payload.explanation: Puppies whine at the door when they need to go to the toilet or want exercise.

payload.snippet: The cat knocks its food bowl off the shelf.
options: Pick up the bowl and refill it at floor level
Leave the food on the floor
Move the bowl to a higher shelf
payload.explanation: Food bowls belong on the floor so cats can eat safely.

payload.snippet: The rabbit's hay rack is empty.
options: Fill the rack with fresh hay
payload.explanation: Rabbits need unlimited hay every day for their digestion.

payload.snippet: The dog's fur is matted and tangled.
options: Wash the dog in the pond
payload.explanation: Regular brushing removes tangles and keeps a dog's coat healthy.

payload.snippet: The bird's cage is very dirty.
options: Clean the cage with warm water
Add more food to cover the dirt
Move the bird to a box
payload.explanation: A clean cage keeps birds healthy and free from disease.

payload.snippet: The guinea pig squeaks and runs to its food bowl.
options: Give the guinea pig fresh vegetables
Tap the cage to calm it down
payload.explanation: Guinea pigs squeak when they are hungry; fresh vegetables are a healthy treat.

payload.snippet: The dog is limping on one front paw.
options: Check the paw for a thorn or cut
Make the dog run to stretch it out
Put a bandage on without looking
Leave it to heal on its own today
payload.explanation: A limp often means something is hurting; checking the paw finds thorns or injuries quickly.

payload.snippet: The cat is sick after eating something outside.
options: Keep the cat calm indoors and call the vet
Give the cat more food to settle its stomach
Put the cat in a bath
payload.explanation: If a cat has eaten something harmful, a vet can advise on the safest next steps.

payload.snippet: The goldfish is swimming sideways near the surface.
options: Test the water quality and call a pet shop for advice
Change all the water at once
Take the fish out and put it in a cup
payload.explanation: Sideways swimming usually signals a water quality problem or swim bladder issue; advice before acting prevents further harm.

payload.snippet: The puppy chews on an electrical cable.
options: Gently redirect the puppy to a chew toy and cover the cable
Put the puppy in another room all day
Wrap the cable in tape and leave it
payload.explanation: Puppies chew instinctively; redirecting to safe toys protects both the pup and the home.

payload.snippet: The rabbit has escaped from its hutch into the garden.
options: Move slowly and calmly to herd the rabbit back into a safe enclosure
Chase the rabbit around the garden quickly
Call the rabbit loudly from indoors
payload.explanation: Rabbits panic easily; slow, calm movement prevents injury and makes recapture easier.

payload.snippet: The dog refuses to eat its food for two days.
options: Take the dog to the vet for a check-up
Switch to a completely new food right away
Give the dog human leftovers to tempt it
Reduce the portion size and see if it eats less
payload.explanation: Two days without eating is a sign something may be wrong; a vet check rules out illness.

payload.snippet: The cat's claws are getting very long.
options: Trim the claws with special pet nail clippers
File the claws with a nail file
Let the cat scratch on the furniture
Cover the cat's paws with socks
payload.explanation: Regular claw trimming prevents the claws curling into the paw pads, which is very painful.

payload.snippet: The hamster has not come out of its nest for two days.
options: Check that the hamster is still eating and drinking; if not, consult a vet
Move all the bedding to find it
Shine a bright torch into the nest
Shake the cage gently to wake it
payload.explanation: Hamsters sleep a lot but should still eat and drink; a vet call is wise if signs of life are absent.

payload.snippet: The dog is scratching its ears constantly.
options: Examine the ear for redness or smell and visit the vet
Pour water into the ear to soothe it
Ignore it for a few weeks
Give the dog a bath and hope it clears
payload.explanation: Persistent ear scratching often means infection or ear mites, which need veterinary treatment.

payload.snippet: The pet tortoise has not moved or eaten for three days in winter.
options: Check the temperature of the enclosure and ensure it is warm enough
Give the tortoise a cold bath to wake it
Move the tortoise to the garden
Offer the tortoise meat to increase its energy
payload.explanation: Tortoises slow down dramatically if they are cold; maintaining the correct temperature range keeps them active and eating.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's ball rolls into your garden.
options: Take the ball back to your neighbour
payload.explanation: Returning something that belongs to someone else is the kind thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour looks sad sitting on the doorstep.
options: Say hello and ask if they are okay
payload.explanation: Noticing when someone is sad and checking on them is being a good neighbour.

payload.snippet: The elderly lady next door is carrying heavy shopping bags.
options: Offer to carry the bags for her
Tell her to use a trolley
payload.explanation: Helping with heavy loads is a kind and thoughtful thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's dog has escaped through the garden fence.
options: Close your own gate and do nothing
payload.explanation: Letting the owner know quickly is the safest way to help get the dog back.

payload.snippet: The baby next door is crying very loudly late at night.
options: Leave it to the parents to handle
Knock on the door at midnight
payload.explanation: Babies cry — parents know what to do. Knocking late at night would disturb everyone.

payload.snippet: You see your neighbour drop their keys and keep walking.
options: Pick up the keys and call out to them
Put them through a random letterbox
payload.explanation: Calling out and returning dropped keys is a helpful and honest thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's washing has blown off the line into your garden.
options: Hand the laundry back over the fence
Leave them on the wet ground
payload.explanation: Returning things that blow into your garden is a neighbourly and honest act.

payload.snippet: A new family moves in next door with a child your age.
options: Smile and say hello when you see them
Stare at them and say nothing
payload.explanation: Welcoming new neighbours with a friendly hello helps them feel at home.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's cat is stuck up a tree.
options: Tell your neighbour so they can help
Try to climb the tree yourself
Walk away and forget about it
payload.explanation: Telling the owner is the safest first step — they can decide how to help.

payload.snippet: You accidentally kick your ball through your neighbour's window.
options: Tell your parent and go apologise straight away
Run inside and pretend it wasn't you
Wait to see if they notice
payload.explanation: Owning up to accidents quickly is always the right thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour asks you not to play loud music near their window while their baby sleeps.
options: Move further away or play more quietly
Argue that you were there first
Play music anyway because it's your garden
payload.explanation: Being considerate of others' needs, especially babies sleeping, is good neighbourly behaviour.

payload.snippet: The man next door slips on ice at the bottom of his steps.
options: Ask if he is hurt and tell your parent
Tell him he should have been more careful
payload.explanation: Checking if someone is hurt and getting a grown-up is the caring and sensible thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour leaves a note asking you to keep the shared path clear of bikes.
options: Move your bike and say thank you for letting you know
Leave the bikes where they are
Take down the note and ignore it
payload.explanation: Respecting shared spaces and being gracious about polite requests keeps neighbours happy.

payload.snippet: You notice the lights in the house next door have been on all night and no one has opened the curtains.
options: Mention it to a parent or trusted adult
Break a window to check inside
payload.explanation: Mentioning an unusual observation to a trusted adult is the safe and sensible action.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour grows prize roses and you accidentally break one off playing in the garden.
options: Tell your parent and offer to apologise to the neighbour
Push the broken flower back into the soil
Throw it away and say nothing
payload.explanation: Honesty and offering an apology shows responsibility and earns respect.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour brings home-baked biscuits to your door as a thank-you for helping them.
options: Say thank you warmly and share them with your family
Say you don't want them and close the door
Give them back and say you don't eat biscuits
payload.explanation: Accepting a kind gift graciously and saying thank you makes the other person feel appreciated.

payload.snippet: A parcel is delivered to your house that is addressed to your neighbour.
options: Bring the parcel next door as soon as possible
Open it to see what's inside
Leave it outside in the rain
payload.explanation: Returning a wrongly delivered parcel quickly is honest and considerate.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour is away on holiday and their wheelie bin is blocking the shared path.
options: Move the bin to the side so people can pass
Leave it blocking the path — not your problem
Go through their garden to move it further away
payload.explanation: Helping with a small inconvenience when a neighbour is away is a kind community gesture.

payload.snippet: You see two children from the street throwing stones at your neighbour's fence.
options: Tell a trusted adult what you saw
Say nothing because they might bully you
payload.explanation: Telling a trusted adult about property damage is the right action — it's not telling tales, it's being responsible.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's child falls off their bike right in front of you.
options: Check if they are hurt and help them up
Go home and tell your parents later
payload.explanation: Stopping to help someone who has fallen is a basic act of kindness.

payload.snippet: The photo came out very dark.
payload.explanation: Photos taken in dark places are hard to see. More light makes them much better.

payload.snippet: The picture is all blurry.
options: Hold the camera very still and try again
payload.explanation: Blurry photos happen when the camera moves. Keeping still helps the camera capture a sharp image.

payload.snippet: Your finger is covering part of the lens.
options: Move your finger away from the lens
payload.explanation: Covering the lens blocks the view. Always check your fingers are clear before pressing the button.

payload.snippet: The sun is shining right into the camera lens.
options: Turn so the sun is behind you
Close your eyes and press the button
Take the photo straight into the sun
payload.explanation: Shooting into the sun makes photos very bright and hard to see. Keeping the sun behind you gives a much clearer picture.

payload.snippet: The dog keeps moving every time you press the button.
options: Wait until the dog is sitting still
Take a photo of something else
Put the dog in a box
payload.explanation: Moving subjects come out blurry. Waiting for a still moment helps you get a sharp, clear photo.

payload.snippet: The photo shows the inside of your pocket.
options: Take the phone out properly and try again
Keep taking photos in your pocket
payload.explanation: Accidental pocket photos happen when the camera button is pressed by mistake. Taking the phone out first solves it.

payload.snippet: You want to take a photo of a rainbow but it is very far away.
options: Zoom in to make the rainbow look bigger
payload.explanation: Zooming brings distant things closer in the frame so you can see them better in the photo.

payload.snippet: Your photo has a big shadow across it.
options: Move so your shadow does not fall on the subject
payload.explanation: Shadows in photos can block the subject. Moving your position so the shadow falls elsewhere fixes it.

payload.snippet: The colours in the photo look orange and strange indoors.
options: Turn on more lights or open the curtains
Take the photo in the dark
Paint the room a different colour
payload.explanation: Indoor lights can make photos look orange. More daylight or brighter lights help colours look natural.

payload.snippet: You want a photo of your whole family but there is no one to press the button.
options: Use the timer setting so the camera takes the photo automatically
Hold the camera very far away
payload.explanation: The timer lets you set the camera down, get in position, and have the camera take the photo on its own.

payload.snippet: The photo has too many people's heads cut off at the top.
options: Step back further so everyone fits in the frame
payload.explanation: Stepping back gives more room in the frame so everyone's head and body can fit into the picture.

payload.snippet: It is night time and everything looks black in the photo.
options: Turn on a light near the subject
Close your eyes to take the photo
Use the photo as a bookmark
payload.explanation: Cameras need light to capture an image. A nearby light source brightens the subject so it shows up clearly.

payload.snippet: You want a photo of a butterfly but it flies away before you can press the button.
options: Wait very quietly and still for the butterfly to land again
Chase the butterfly waving your arms
Take a photo of a flower instead
payload.explanation: Patience is important in nature photography. Staying quiet and still gives wild creatures time to settle.

payload.snippet: The photo has a big pole growing out of someone's head.
options: Move to a different angle where the pole is not behind the person
payload.explanation: Distracting objects in the background can be removed simply by changing your position slightly.

payload.snippet: You take a photo of your drawing but the paper looks very white and bright.
options: Move to indirect light instead of direct sunshine
Hold the drawing behind a curtain
payload.explanation: Direct sunlight bleaches out white paper. Soft indirect light preserves the colours and details of your drawing.

payload.snippet: Your selfie only shows the top of your head.
options: Hold the camera a little higher and tilt it down slightly
Take a photo of just your hair
Ask a friend to take it instead
payload.explanation: Holding the camera slightly above eye level and tilting it down creates a flattering angle that shows your whole face.

payload.snippet: The photo is too small to see the details of your model you built.
options: Move the camera closer to fill the frame with the model
payload.explanation: Getting closer to a subject fills the frame with detail, making it much easier to see in the finished photo.

payload.snippet: You want to photograph the moon but it looks like a tiny white dot.
options: Use as much zoom as possible and keep the camera very still
Throw the camera up in the air
Wait until the moon is bigger
payload.explanation: The moon is very far away; maximum zoom combined with a very steady hold gets the best detail.

payload.snippet: Your birthday photo has red glowing eyes.
options: Turn off the flash and use a lamp nearby instead
Add red sunglasses to the photo
payload.explanation: Red eye is caused by flash reflecting off the retina. Using ambient light instead of direct flash eliminates the effect.

payload.snippet: The background of the photo is very messy and distracting.
options: Move the subject to a cleaner spot or step closer to fill the frame
Add more mess to make it fair
payload.explanation: A clean or simple background keeps the viewer's attention on the subject rather than the clutter behind them.

payload.snippet: You are doing a puzzle and cannot find the last piece.
options: Look under the table and cushions where it might have fallen
Give up and throw the puzzle away
Colour in a piece of paper to replace it
payload.explanation: Puzzle pieces often fall under furniture. Checking nearby surfaces and the floor is always worth a try.

payload.snippet: Two puzzle pieces look exactly the same but one does not fit.
options: Try both and use the one that clicks in smoothly
Force the wrong one in with your fist
Cut the piece to make it fit
payload.explanation: Similar-looking pieces are common in puzzles. Gently trying each one and feeling for the click tells you which is correct.

payload.snippet: You accidentally sit on one puzzle piece and it bends.
options: Gently flatten it under a heavy book
Keep it bent so you know which one it is
Hide it at the back of the box
payload.explanation: A bent piece can often be flattened by placing something heavy on it for a few minutes.

payload.snippet: The puzzle box has a picture but the pieces are all face down.
options: Turn all the pieces face up before you start
Build the puzzle with the pieces face down
Put all the brown pieces together
Give up because you cannot see the picture
payload.explanation: Turning all pieces face up first gives you the whole picture to work with and makes it much easier to match shapes and colours.

payload.snippet: You are halfway done but need to go for dinner.
options: Leave the puzzle on the table and come back after dinner
Sweep it all back into the box
Take the puzzle to the dinner table
Ask your mum to finish it

post photos of the binned books online to shame the school

phone the police because dad is going to be late for work
payload.explanation: A polite knock now is faster than a note or police call.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's cat keeps using your mum's vegetable patch as a toilet, and your dog ate something from the soil last week and was very unwell afterwards.
options: ask the neighbour and add cat-deterrent plants around the bed
throw the cat over the fence whenever you see her there
feed the cat treats so she stops hunting in your garden
stop growing vegetables because of one neighbour's cat
payload.explanation: Honest chat plus deterrent plants protects the dog and the friendship.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's house alarm has been going off all morning and they're away on holiday for two weeks, and the noise is giving your gran a terrible headache.

phone the police because the noise is upsetting your gran
climb their fence to see if you can switch it off
ignore it because the alarm will run out of battery eventually

payload.snippet: The neighbour with three small dogs lets them out at five every morning to bark in the garden, and your dad has finally lost patience after a month of it.

go round at five tomorrow morning to film the dogs barking
complain to the council about the morning noise straight away
buy the dogs treats so they like you and bark less
payload.explanation: Daytime calm chats land better than five-am confrontations.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's tree has grown right over your back garden and now half the lawn never gets sun, and your mum says the grass is dying off in patches.

chop the branches off without asking and clear up later
let the lawn die and lay artificial grass instead
report the tree to the council as overgrowth
payload.explanation: Asking first respects the tree and the neighbourly relationship.

payload.snippet: You see your neighbour's nine-year-old climbing out of her bedroom window onto the porch roof, and you're not sure if she's playing or trying to run away.
options: call up to her gently and tell her parents about it
shout at her to get down before she falls off
video it on your phone in case she falls afterwards
wait to see what happens before getting involved
payload.explanation: Telling her parents now prevents either play or running away ending badly.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour brought you a homemade pie because you helped with her shopping, but you're vegetarian and the pie is full of beef and onion gravy.
options: thank her warmly and quietly give the pie to your dad
tell her you're vegetarian so she remembers next time
throw the pie out and never mention it to her
eat the pie anyway so you don't hurt her feelings
payload.explanation: A warm thanks now and a gentle mention next time both work.

payload.snippet: Your elderly neighbour confides that her son hasn't visited her for two years and she's lonely, but she made you promise not to mention it to your mum.
options: encourage her to ring her son and check in on her regularly
keep the secret and forget she ever mentioned it
tell mum anyway because it's too sad to keep quiet
ring the son yourself from her phone without asking
payload.explanation: Encouraging her own call respects her wishes and her loneliness.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour put up a tall fence right along the path you both share, and now your bins won't fit through the gap to reach the front for collection.
options: show her the bin problem and ask for a small adjustment
push the fence over because it shouldn't be there
carry bins through the house every collection day forever
report her fence to planning permission straight away
payload.explanation: Showing the bin problem makes the issue obvious and fixable.

payload.snippet: The new family next door has a teenage daughter who keeps blasting music from her car at half past seven every morning before she leaves for college.
options: leave a friendly note explaining your baby brother sleeps through that time
smash her wing mirror so she's late and doesn't bother again
blast your own music back at her each evening loudly
post a warning on the street's WhatsApp group anonymously

payload.snippet: Your next-door neighbour's son just got his first car and you can smell strong petrol fumes coming from their open garage every evening this week.

ring the fire brigade about a possible petrol leak nearby
open all your windows to clear the smell from your house
wait a week and see if the smell goes away on its own
payload.explanation: Parents popping round is faster and less alarming than fire engines.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour offers to mind your puppy while you're at football, but her own dog is aggressive and your puppy is still too young to defend himself properly.
options: thank her and explain you'd rather book a proper dog sitter
agree because she's the friendly neighbour and it's free
agree but ask her to keep the dogs in separate rooms
say yes once and never let her dogsit again afterwards
payload.explanation: Honest declines keep your puppy safe and the friendship intact.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour asks to borrow your dad's drill for ten minutes, but last time she borrowed his ladder she kept it for two months before returning it.
options: lend it but agree on a return time before she takes it
lend it without saying anything and hope she returns it
refuse to lend it because of the ladder problem before
lend her a different drill so dad's stays at home safe

payload.snippet: You spotted your neighbour's young child wandering the street alone in pyjamas at half past seven on a Sunday morning while everyone else was still asleep.
options: walk her home and knock loudly until a parent answers
leave her be because she clearly came out by herself
video her so you have proof for the parents later
take her into your house and wait for someone to notice
payload.explanation: Knocking until a parent answers reunites her safely and quickly.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour's car alarm goes off every time a heavy lorry rumbles past your road, and tonight it's already woken your gran up three times after midnight.
options: ring the neighbour now because they probably can't hear it
bang on their door until they come out to disable it
throw a stone at the car to set off the alarm fully
complain to the council in writing on Monday morning
payload.explanation: A phone call lets them switch it off before the next lorry.

payload.snippet: Your neighbour invites your family to a barbecue but you know they're struggling with money, and your mum says they shouldn't be feeding the whole street.
options: go but bring a homemade salad and dessert to share
go empty-handed because they invited you not the other way
make an excuse so they save money by not feeding you
go but only eat a tiny bit so they have leftovers
payload.explanation: Bringing food turns the barbecue into a proper shared meal.

payload.snippet: You took a candid photo of your friend laughing during lunch and it's really sweet, but she's got food round her mouth and would hate it being shared.
options: show her first and only post it if she gives the okay
post it because it captures a genuine happy moment
share it just to your close-friends story so it's smaller
send it to her in private and tease her about her face
payload.explanation: Showing first respects her face and keeps the friendship safe.

payload.snippet: Your photography club project is due Monday and the best landscape shot you took has another kid's little brother in the corner without his parents' permission.
options: crop the brother out and submit the landscape clean
submit it because it's mostly landscape anyway
blur his face and hope nobody notices the change
ask the kid if he minds and skip his parents
payload.explanation: Cropping protects the child and keeps the landscape strong.

payload.snippet: Your dad asks you to take a family Christmas photo on his proper camera, but you've never used it and he's already pouring everyone a drink in the lounge.
options: ask him for a two-minute tutorial before everyone gathers
take the photo on auto and hope it comes out fine
use your phone instead and email it to him afterwards
say no and ask a relative who knows the camera
payload.explanation: A two-minute tutorial saves a blurred family Christmas memory.

payload.snippet: Your friend wants you to take photos of her in her new gymnastics leotard for her social media, but she's twelve and her dad keeps her account private for safety.
options: say yes only if her dad sees the photos before posting
take the photos because they're just for her account
take them but say she shouldn't post them publicly
refuse to take any photos of her in the leotard at all
payload.explanation: Dad's preview is the safety system that's already in place.

payload.snippet: You sneak a photo of your teacher tripping over a bin during assembly and the whole class wants you to AirDrop it round the year group right now.
options: delete it because it would humiliate her in front of everyone
share it because it's just a funny harmless moment
share it only to your three closest friends quietly
keep it on your phone but promise not to share it
payload.explanation: Adult humiliation spreads fast — delete now, not later.

payload.snippet: Your gran asks you to scan old family photos but one of the boxes contains pictures of relatives who've passed away, and your mum gets emotional seeing them suddenly.
options: scan a few and show mum gently before going through them all
scan them all in one go to get the job done
skip the box and tell gran you couldn't find it
show mum every single photo as you scan them in
payload.explanation: A gentle preview lets mum brace before the harder photos.

payload.snippet: Your friend posts a photo you took of you both at the beach, but she's cropped you out of the picture and only kept herself looking great in it.
options: ask her kindly to credit you as the photographer in the caption
unfollow her and tell other friends what she did
comment publicly that you took the photo so everyone sees
stop taking photos of her ever again from now on
payload.explanation: A kind ask gives her a chance to fix it without drama.

payload.snippet: You're taking photos at your cousin's wedding rehearsal as a favour and your aunt asks if you can also film the speeches with one hand while shooting.
options: say honestly that you can't do both well and suggest one job
agree because she's family and you don't want to upset her
agree but warn the footage and photos might be poor
do it but skip taking photos during the speeches
payload.explanation: Honest limits beat ruined photos and ruined speech footage.

payload.snippet: Your phone storage is full from class trip photos and the museum gift shop has internet, but downloading from cloud will use up your monthly mobile data limit.
options: use the museum's free wifi to back up and free space
delete photos at random until your phone has space
carry on without backing up and hope nothing breaks
switch to mobile data even though it'll cost your parents
payload.explanation: Free wifi in shops is exactly what travel days are for.

payload.snippet: Your school newspaper wants a photo of the football team but the captain is off sick on the only day everyone else is free for the shoot.
options: ask the team if you can reshoot when she's back
take the photo without her and crop her into it later
use last season's photo even though three players have left
leave the team off the newspaper page this issue
payload.explanation: Reshooting honours the captain and gets a real team photo.

payload.snippet: You snapped a great shot of your dog mid-jump but your finger covered the lens slightly, leaving a black smudge on one side of the photo you can't edit out.
options: accept the smudge and use it as a learning lesson on grip
lie and say the smudge is artistic vignetting on purpose

payload.snippet: Your friend wants you to photograph her birthday party but her parents have a strict rule that no children's faces can be posted online without their families' permission.

take them and let the parents sort out permissions later
take backs-of-heads photos so nobody's face is shown
refuse to take any photos because of the parent rules
payload.explanation: Camera-roll-only respects the rule and still captures memories.

payload.snippet: Your gran's eightieth birthday photo album is your responsibility but you accidentally left the camera on the bus on the way home, and the lost property line is closed.

pretend you didn't take any photos at the party
blame your little brother for distracting you on the bus
buy gran a new camera to make up for losing hers

payload.snippet: Your photography teacher wants the class to shoot strangers on the high street for an urban portrait project, but you feel uncomfortable photographing people without asking first.

do it because the teacher said so and grades matter most

payload.snippet: Your friend asks you to delete a group photo because she doesn't like how she looks, but you and four others love the photo and want to keep it as a memory.

keep posting it because the majority wins in the group
delete it from everywhere and tell the others tough luck
edit her out and post the picture without her in it

payload.snippet: Your camera's battery dies just before your nephew's first steps and your phone is charging in the kitchen plug downstairs, two flights away.

borrow your sister's phone without asking permission first

shoot from the pavement and zoom in as best you can
wait until tomorrow when the sunset might be just as good
